text: **An artefact asserts its own provenance, and the assertion is READ FROM THE ARTEFACT, never from a record written beside it.** (vc 2026-08-17, on dc's finding; dc asked whether to strengthen AC-11.4 and the ruling is that this is a different criterion.) **A manifest states what was MEANT to be built; only the artefact can answer what was.** Three states are currently indistinguishable, all measured live and unplanted rather than constructed. **(a) The signed binary cannot name its commit**: `int macos stage` records `commit: <HEAD>` and `traceable: yes` -- where traceable means the working tree is clean -- and never asks when the binaries were BUILT, because `stage` copies them rather than building them. Measured with HEAD at `2026-08-17T15:11:14Z`: `intent` built three hours earlier, `intentd` **forty-two hours** earlier, forty-two hours apart from each other. Commit the tree and the whole chain goes green over bytes from two different earlier trees. **(b) The vendored tree cannot name its source**: `int vendor` compares the vendored files against a manifest that ships beside them and is rewritten by the same act that changes them, so a re-vendor and a local patch produce the identical `27 of 27`; and `devbin_version: 0.1.0` cannot separate them either, because **the field that exists to carry provenance is constant across exactly the thing it must distinguish.** **(c) An UNCOMMITTED REGENERATION is invisible to both** (dc, correcting their own report and vc's explanation of it): a tree that agrees with itself because someone re-derived the record locally is indistinguishable from a tree that agrees because it is correct. Measured at HEAD `702b58f8`: `bin/devbin` is `41017e54` while the manifest committed beside it records `8016f112`, so **a fresh clone reports DIVERGED right now** -- and every local check ran green throughout, over a regenerated manifest that was never committed. Verified by vc that `upstream/main` at `5765c5da` is self-consistent, so nothing broken is published; **that containment is an artefact of hv's CI-budget freeze and is recorded as luck rather than as a control**, because filing it as a save would teach the opposite of what happened. **Requires two things, and the second is what closes (c)**: the artefact carries its own source commit, embedded at build time and read back FROM the binary -- dc's own `staged_version` already argues this one function over, read the version from the BINARY and never from a manifest; and every provenance check compares against what the COMMIT holds rather than the worktree, for the same reason the whiteboard clock guard's check C blocks only on what the commit adds. **This is deliberately NOT folded into AC-11.4.** That row's criterion is _the published hash matching the published bytes_, which stale binaries satisfy perfectly -- the hash is honest and the commit attribution is not. Folding a provenance control under a checksum row would make a green start meaning something the row's text does not say, **which is the third axis (a remedy whose subject is not the report's) arriving inside a remedy.** dc declined to do it unprompted and asked first **MARKER CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (vc): this row carried the doc-check marker, and that made it UNCLOSABLE.** `ac_is_satisfied` returns on the doc-check branch before it ever looks at a covering AT, so **AT-11.5 could go green and this AC would not move**; and the only route the marker leaves is hand-writing a `yes` into this line's own inline satisfaction field, **which is a record written beside the artefact -- the exact form this criterion forbids.** Two routes on paper, zero in the gate, and the one the doc points at is the one the row prohibits. It was marked non-test by copying AC-11.1 to AC-11.4, which genuinely are doc checks; this row then acquired a real instrument and the marker did not follow. **`at lint` reports all rows conform over it.** L5 catches the mirror pairing -- a doc-check AT covering a test-backed AC -- and names the symptom exactly, _"an unclosable contract whose only symptom is a gate that will not move"_; **the reverse pairing produces the identical harm and is not checked.** Reported to hv rather than fixed here: `bin/**` is not vc's to edit. **AND THIS NOTE SATISFIED ITS OWN ROW ON THE FIRST WRITE (vc, caught in the same minute by the marker scan, gate 46 -> 47).** The sentence warning that a hand-written flag would close the row SPELLED the flag, and the parser cannot tell a row's data from a row's prose about its data -- **the document is its own format, so writing about a marker writes the marker.** This week's class again, at the smallest scale it has appeared: the measurement's subject and the report's subject were different, and the output could not tell them apart. **Nothing else in the contract does this today** -- the scan checks the whole table in both directions, and this was the only hit. **The gate cannot catch it: a row that hand-satisfies itself is a row that is satisfied**, and `at lint` reads all rows as conforming either way. **AND THIS ROW HAS NOW DONE IT TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, WITH TWO DIFFERENT TOKENS (vc).** The first note spelled the satisfaction field and CLOSED a row that must not close (gate 46 -> 47). **The note announcing that repair spelled the doc-check marker three times, and `ac_is_nontest` matches it ANYWHERE IN THE LINE (`bin/intent_acceptance:90`), so the repair undid itself and the row was unclosable again -- gate 46 while my own parser said 47.** **The disagreement is the only reason it surfaced, and it surfaced by luck: my scan reads the marker POSITIONALLY (immediately after the id) and the gate reads it anywhere, so for every row where the token appears only in its proper place the two agree exactly -- which is what they had been doing all session.** **Two readers of one format, agreeing until the first row that separates them.** The scan is being corrected to the gate's reading, because a checker that disagrees with the authority about what the data MEANS will keep certifying the authority's answer as its own. **The general form, and it is the day's class at the smallest possible scale: in a document that is its own data format, writing ABOUT a marker writes the marker -- so a note explaining a repair is itself a repair, in whichever direction the token points.**
